title: U.S. warns California about counting some ballots
summary:
The U.S. Justice Department sent a warning to election officials in California. It says they could be investigated if they count ballots from people the government thinks are not U.S. citizens.

Only U.S. citizens may vote in federal elections. It is a crime for noncitizens to vote in them.

The letter came on Friday, October 16. It was sent to officials in Los Angeles County and to California's top election official, Secretary of State Shirley Weber.

One day earlier, the Trump administration sued California. It wants the state to hold back mail ballots from about 20,000 people it calls "likely" noncitizens until their status is checked. Weber said the government has given no proof for its list.

The Justice Department says 50 people have been charged this year with voting as noncitizens. Earlier this year, the government said Nevada had 1,500 noncitizen voters, but checks found zero.

The election is on November 3.
why_it_matters: Fair rules for counting votes help make sure every eligible person's vote is counted the right way.

keywords.explanation: Election officials are the people who run elections and count the votes.
Ballots are the papers or forms people use to vote.
Citizens are people who officially belong to a country and have rights there, like voting.
Federal means having to do with the national government of the whole United States.
Sued means took someone to court to settle a disagreement.
Proof is information that shows something is true.

background_read: In the United States, only citizens are allowed to vote in federal elections.
Each state runs its own elections, including mailing out and counting ballots.
The U.S. Justice Department is the part of the national government that makes sure federal laws are followed.
